title: Overview of Audit of Public Sector Undertakings
outcomes: Explain the government audit framework and the C&AG's role.
Distinguish financial and compliance audit of PSUs.
Apply propriety audit principles and understand C&AG reporting.

meta.exam_tip: Name the audit type (financial, compliance, performance, propriety) before analysing a PSU case.

concepts.title: Framework of government audit and the C&AG
body: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (C&AG), under Articles 148–151 of the Constitution and the C&AG (DPC) Act, 1971, audits receipts and expenditure of the Union and States and of bodies substantially financed by government, including government companies and corporations.

For government companies, the C&AG appoints the statutory auditor (a chartered accountant firm), issues directions on the manner of audit, conducts supplementary or test audit, and comments on or supplements the auditor's report (section 143(5)–(7) of the Companies Act).
C&AG reports are laid before Parliament or state legislatures and examined by the Public Accounts Committee and Committee on Public Undertakings.
concepts.analogy: Public money needs a public auditor — the C&AG.
concepts.work: A statutory auditor of a PSU reports on C&AG directions under section 143(5).

concepts.title: Financial and compliance audit of PSUs
body: PSU audit elements: auditor (C&AG and appointed auditors), responsible party, intended users (legislature, public), subject matter and criteria. Principles include independence, objectivity, professional judgement, communication and quality control.
Financial audit gives an opinion on whether financial statements present a true and fair view in line with the framework.
Compliance audit checks whether activities, transactions and information follow authorities — laws, rules, regulations, budgets, policies and contracts — and principles of sound financial management.
concepts.analogy: Financial audit asks "are the numbers right?"; compliance audit asks "were the rules followed?".
concepts.work: A compliance audit checks whether procurement followed tender rules.

concepts.title: Performance and comprehensive audit
body: Performance audit is an independent assessment of whether government undertakings, programmes or systems operate with economy, efficiency and effectiveness (the 3Es), and whether there is room for improvement.
Planning involves choosing topics on risk and significance, defining objectives and criteria, designing methods (data analysis, field visits, surveys) and reporting findings with recommendations.
Comprehensive audit of PSUs appraises overall performance: achievement of targets, cost control, capital planning, idle capacity, pricing, delays and overruns, and investment returns.
concepts.analogy: Performance audit judges value for money.
concepts.work: A plant 50% over budget and 18 months late is a classic performance audit finding.

concepts.title: Propriety audit and C&AG reporting
body: Propriety audit examines whether expenditure meets standards of financial propriety: spending no more than the occasion demands, no authority using powers to benefit itself, public money not used for any person's benefit unless allowed, and charges for services rendered by government recovered.
It looks at wisdom, faithfulness and economy of decisions, not just legality.
C&AG audit reports compile findings from financial, compliance and performance audits; they are submitted to the President or Governor and laid before the legislature for scrutiny.
concepts.analogy: Legal is not always proper — propriety audit asks if it was right to spend.
concepts.work: Lavish spending on events by a PSU may be legal but improper.

illustrations.title: A performance audit finding
illustrations.q: A state PSU built a power plant budgeted at ₹100 crore and 30 months; it cost ₹145 crore and took 48 months. Compute the overrun and delay and suggest the performance audit angle.

illustrations.q: Comment from a propriety audit angle: (a) a PSU spent heavily on a chairman's farewell party; (b) a contract was awarded to a relative of a director without tender; (c) a costly car was bought for an officer not entitled to it.

viva.q: What is the role of C&AG in government company audits?
viva.model: Appointing the statutory auditor, issuing directions, conducting supplementary or test audit and commenting on the audit report.
Financial audit opines on whether statements give a true and fair view; compliance audit checks adherence to laws, rules and other authorities.

viva.q: State a canon of financial propriety.
viva.model: Expenditure should be no more than the occasion demands, and no authority should use its powers to benefit itself.
Parliament or state legislatures through the Public Accounts Committee and the Committee on Public Undertakings.

cases.title: State Transport Corporation
cases.case: A state road transport corporation's new buses cost 20% above market rates due to a single-vendor order. 30% of the fleet is idle. A CA firm appointed by C&AG audits its accounts, and C&AG plans a performance review.

mcqs.q: Paying 20% above market rates relates to:
mcqs.explain: Least-cost acquisition. In practice: tender review.

mcqs.q: 30% idle fleet indicates a problem with:
The CA firm's report must also address:
mcqs.explain: Government company requirement. In practice: sub-directions.
mcqs.topic: Framework of government audit and the C&AG

mcqs.explain: Procurement rules and fairness. In practice: report findings.
